prompt: The Internet makes it easy for businesses to obtain information and develop profiles of customers that the businesses use to
explanation: Target markets. In electronic commerce, customers leave behind bits of information each time they visit a site, such as their names, addresses, credit-card numbers, preferences, and purchase decisions. Business-es accumulate this information and develop profiles of customers in order to know who their customers are and what they want. Then, businesses use the profiles to more effectively target their specific markets, the group of people who are most likely to buy their products. Businesses do not develop profiles of customers in order to create software, conduct research, or secure transactions.

prompt: Buyer Jones is negotiating a contract to purchase a large quantity of products from Seller Brown. There are several things Jones wants Brown to agree to before Jones will agree to buy. What is this buyer asking for?
explanation: Concessions. Concessions are items granted by one party to another in order to reach agreement. In a purchasing situation, the buyer might want to negotiate such concessions as delivery by a certain date, favorable shipping terms, or an extended payment period. Obtaining concessions is usually part of the negotiating process. Commitments are promises of various kinds. Commissions are sums earned by sales-persons on their sales. Consequences are the results of actions.

prompt: Interest an online business earns from its bank accounts is included in which category of the profit-and-loss statement?
explanation: Revenue. The revenue category of the profit-and-loss statement includes the total amount of money earned by an online business. It includes interest earned from bank accounts, returns on investments, sale of assets, and sales of the business's goods and services. Assets are anything of value that the business owns and are included on a balance statement. Net income is the money remaining after operating expenses are subtracted from gross profit. Gross sales is the total value of goods or services sold in a period of time.

prompt: One of the main disadvantages of using e-mail is that it lacks
explanation: Confidentiality. E-mails are about as confidential as postcards: Anyone exposed to them can read them. They can even be intercepted in transit over the Internet, unless they are encrypted. Sensitive financial and medical information can, therefore, fall into the wrong hands. E-mail is a reliable way of sending information quickly. Most legitimate e-mail that is sent from businesses or individuals to other businesses and individ-uals is authentic and believable.

prompt: Internet businesses use budgets to estimate how they will
explanation: Spend their money. A budget estimates how an Internet business will earn and spend its money. Businesses use budgets to estimate how they will spend the money they earn as income. Businesses have expenses, and budgets help businesses plan how to allocate income in order to pay those expenses. Businesses do not use budgets to calculate their assets, file their taxes, or depreciate their assets.

prompt: Who is responsible for developing a quality culture in a brick-and-click business?
explanation: All employees. A quality culture cannot exist in a brick-and-click business unless all employees are involved. Although some employees are more directly involved, everyone must participate. For example, management must provide the guidance and direction as well as the tools necessary for employees to do quality work. The production staff must do their best to produce a quality product, and salespeople must provide quality service to customers. Support personnel, such as accounting clerks and delivery people, also must be committed to doing a quality job. Everyone must do their part and work together to develop a quality culture.

prompt: Which of the following is an ethical issue that an online business manager might encounter:
explanation: Conflict of interest. Managers might encounter a conflict of interest if they are unable to be objective when making decisions about employees. For example, if they are friends with an employee, they might not want to give that person a negative performance evaluation even though it is justified. In those situations, managers should remove themselves in order to be ethical and allow a manager who is not a friend of the employee to conduct the evaluation. Balance of trade is the difference between the value of a nation's exports and its imports. Span of control is the number of workers reporting to a manager. Return on invest-ment is income received from an investment in a business.

prompt: E-businesses study information about consumers' lifestyles, incomes, and ages in order to identify the target market and develop appropriate
explanation: Purchasing policies. E-businesses want to know as much as possible about their target markets in order to provide the goods and services that consumers want. E-businesses build their purchasing policies around the wants and needs of their target markets. Staff levels are the number of employees a company needs to operate effectively. Business policies are statements outlining practices the business follows. Inventory control involves keeping track of the amount of stock on hand, sold, and on order.

prompt: What is the main reason why a company might decide to host its own web site?
choices: The company has employees who have web-hosting skills.
The company wants to have direct control of the web server.
It is more cost effective for a company to host its own site.
Employees are available to work 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
explanation: The company wants to have direct control of the web server. Companies often do not want to give control of their resources to an outside source. When customers or clients need information, companies want to be able to access it immediately. By having someone "in-house," companies are able to reach the person or department immediately to rectify a situation or remedy a problem. Most companies do not have employees within their company who have the skills necessary to host a company's web site. It is often less expensive to hire a web host than for the company to host its own site. Businesses usually do not have employees available to work around the clock and would have to hire additional employees to cover all shifts.

prompt: Which of the following is a standard function of most spreadsheet software programs:
explanation: Performing financial calculations. Spreadsheet software enables businesses to perform accounting, finan-cial, and other mathematical functions. A user can enter numerical information in rows and columns, and the software will perform various calculations or analyses. For example, spreadsheet programs can calculate sales forecasts and develop budget projections. Presentation software is used to create slide presentations. Desktop publishing software is used to prepare promotional brochures. Database software is used to manage database files.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why e-businesses should evaluate speculative risks:
choices: To determine the potential for loss
To reduce the possibility of theft
To estimate the level of property damage
explanation: To determine the potential for loss. Speculative risks are chances of loss that may result in loss, no change, or gain. When a business takes a speculative risk, there is always the possibility of failure. Therefore, before taking speculative risks, businesses usually evaluate them in order to determine the potential for loss. Businesses may decide not to take the risk because the potential for loss is too high. Businesses cannot obtain insurance for speculative risks. Businesses usually purchase insurance to cover losses due to theft or property damage.

prompt: Secure sockets layer (SSL) creates a secure connection between the customer's Internet browser and the
explanation: Merchant's web site. Secure sockets layer (SSL) scrambles sensitive credit-card information before it is electronically transferred from the customer's Internet browser to the merchant's web site. Its counterpart, secure electronic transaction (SET), also creates a secure connection; but the account information goes directly to the customer's credit-card company, thereby, protecting the consumer from unscrupulous merchants who engage in fraud. Neither the customer's Internet service provider (ISP) nor the certification authority receive the credit-card information. The ISP provides the connection that makes the transaction possible. The certification authority issues digital certificates, guaranteeing that the merchant is who s/he claims to be.

prompt: One disadvantage to the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act of 2000 is that
choices: individuals using electronic signatures are charged a service fee.
a computer hacker could intercept the signature and use it illegally.
electronic signatures are not considered legal in confirming contracts.
it requires electronic signatures to gain governmental approval before each use.
explanation: A computer hacker could intercept the signature and use it illegally. Even with privacy protection in place, it is possible for someone to breech security and use electronic signatures without the owner's permission. Credit-card applications, loans, and many other business arrangements are now done on the Internet, and there are no standards to verify the signature. The Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act does not specify that service fees are charged for using electronic signatures. Electronic signatures are considered legal as a method to finalize a contractual agreement. Governmental approval is not required before each use of electronic signatures.

prompt: Before an Internet business and a customer can enter into a valid contract, the offer to do something in return for payment must be
explanation: Accepted. Contracts are agreements between two or more parties stating that one party is to do something in return for something provided by another party. Several elements must be present for a contract to be valid. First, one party must make an offer to do something such as sell a product for a certain price and deliver it on a certain date. Then, the other party must accept that offer. A valid contract cannot be formed unless the offer is accepted. The offer may be made verbally or in writing. Express and implied are types of contracts that may be formed once the offer is accepted.

prompt: Which of the following laws pertains to overtime pay for employees:
explanation: Fair Labor Standards Act. The Fair Labor Standards Act contains provisions that cover overtime pay. The act states that businesses must pay hourly employees one-and-a-half times the base rate for working over-time or provide them with a comparable amount of time off. If an employee worked four hours, s/he would be paid for six hours or given six hours off at a later time. Businesses often try to schedule enough employees to cover each shift so they are not required to pay overtime, which can add up to a costly expense. The Equal Pay Act requires men and women to receive equal pay for doing the same work. The Tax Reform Act revised the tax code. The Equal Employment Opportunity Act made it illegal for businesses to discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, sex, or national origin.

prompt: A complex written report may include an appendix. The purpose of an appendix is to
choices: present a brief summary of the report.
list all of the sources used in writing
state the problem and research methods.
include support materials that might help the the report. reader.
explanation: Include support materials that might help the reader. The appendix is placed at the end of the report and might include such items as a copy of a survey instrument or correspondence. A brief summary of the report is a synopsis or executive summary. The problem statement and research methods are part of the introduc-tion. The bibliography lists the sources used in the report.

prompt: A supervisor has given instructions for performing a complex new skill and demonstrated the skill for an employee. What should be the next step?
choices: Let the employee practice the new skill
Ask the employee to teach the skill to others
Assume the employee can now perform the new skill
Test the employee's ability to perform the new skill
explanation: Let the employee practice the new skill. The employee should be given the opportunity to practice a new task or skill before s/he is responsible for its successful completion. Testing should occur after the employee has had the chance to practice the skill. A supervisor should always make sure employees understand instructions and can perform a skill satisfactorily before asking them to teach others.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an online business behaving unethically when it communicates information to customers:
choices: Providing detailed data in chart form
explanation: Deliberately trying to confuse customers. Online businesses are behaving unethically when they deliberately try to confuse customers by providing complex information that will be difficult to understand. Because cus-tomers may have trouble understanding the information, they may be mislead about the product's capabilities. Businesses have an obligation to behave ethically and provide customers with all the accurate information they need to make good buying decisions. Businesses are behaving ethically when they refuse to publicize confi-dential data. It is ethical to send e-mails to customers unless the customers ask to be removed from the mail-ing list. Providing detailed data in chart form often makes complex information easier to understand.

prompt: What has Dell.com eliminated by selling computers directly to customers through its web site?
explanation: Intermediaries. By selling directly to customers, Dell.com has eliminated the intermediaries, including ship-ping companies and various electronics retailers, that would normally move its goods and services to the consumer or industrial user. It has not eliminated security risks because there is always a chance that hackers can break into Dell's database and steal sensitive information. Nor has it eliminated the need for inventory control because it is an important part of keeping track of the computers it has on hand, sold, and on order. The Internet has actually increased competition because it has opened up new opportunities for e-tailers to sell computers to people all over the world.

prompt: Which of the following is a direct channel of distribution for consumer goods and services:
explanation: Producer to ultimate consumer. With this route, goods and services move straight from the producer to the ultimate consumer. It is the simplest of all channels. Although producer to industrial user is a direct route, it is used for industrial rather than consumer goods and services. The producer to retailer to ultimate consumer channel and the producer to distributor to consumer channel are considered indirect channels because they involve the use of intermediaries.

prompt: Wholesalers and e-tailers who buy goods through channels of distribution that are not authorized by the manufacturer of the goods are buying on the __________ market.
explanation: Gray. Wholesalers and e-tailers who buy goods from unauthorized distributors often are able to obtain the goods at a lower price and pass that savings on to customers. The practice usually is considered unethical because the manufacturer and its authorized distributors ultimately lose money. Consumers also may suffer because purchases made from unauthorized dealers may not be covered by the manufacturer's warranty or be eligible for service. The mass market is the entire market. Importing is buying goods and services from other nations. The foreign market is the market in other countries.

prompt: Which express mail service might an online store use if it needs to ship a few packages quickly?
explanation: FedEx. Express mail services such as FedEx, UPS, Airborne Express, or Emery Worldwide specialize in air transportation and overnight delivery. Although more expensive than other forms of transportation, they are widely recognized as the quickest. Pipelines are used to transport oil and natural gas, not packages. Parcel Post is the U.S. Postal Service's fourth-class mail—very affordable but not very quick. Water transportation, although reliable in some instances, is a very slow way to ship products across waters.

prompt: A supplier prepares an invoice with terms of 3/10, net 30 on an order of four items at $178.50 each. What is the total due if the customer takes the discount?
explanation: $692.58. Invoices list the quantity of items purchased, unit price, and terms that indicate when payment is expected. In this situation, there are four items at $178.50 each for a total of $714 ($178.50 x 4 = $714). The terms are 3/10, net 30, which means the customer may take a 3% discount if the invoice is paid within 10 days of the invoice date. To calculate the discount, multiply the net amount by 3% ($714 x 3% or .03 = $21.42). Subtract this figure from the net amount to calculate the total after discount ($714.00 – $21.42 = $692.58).

prompt: What factor must store personnel consider when determining the storage needs for an online apparel outlet?
explanation: Stock turnover rates. Stock turnover rate refers to the average time it takes to sell and replace inventory within a specific time frame. By knowing the stock turnover rate of the inventory, store personnel can better determine how much storage is needed for the product and how long the product will be stored before it is sold. Generally, the higher the stock turnover rate for a specific item, the less storage space is needed. Carrier delivery charges are not necessarily a factor considered when determining storage needs. Many online stores have personnel in other departments that negotiate delivery terms with the carriers. Vendor collusion refers to losses that occur upon delivery of products (e.g., shortages, theft). Inventory valuation refers to the cumulative dollar value of all inventory.

prompt: A small brick-and-click has purchased merchandise for the summer season, but it must take possession of the merchandise in February. The owner needs to store the merchandise for a short time but does not have adequate space. Which of the following would be the best option for the owner to choose:
explanation: Public warehouse. These facilities are available to any business that will pay for their use and are available for short or long periods of time. A private warehouse is owned by a business for its own use and can be expensive to build and maintain. A bonded warehouse stores products that require payment of a federal tax. Distribution centers consolidate large orders from various sources and redistribute them as separate orders.

prompt: What should e-tailers do when they detect shortages in shipments of merchandise?
explanation: Notify vendors. E-tailers should notify vendors when they detect discrepancies such as shortages in ship-ments of merchandise. By notifying vendors, e-tailers are able to make arrangements for the remainder of the order to be shipped, or for the amount of the shortage to be deducted from the invoice. E-tailers do not need to reorder the goods or to return the goods that were delivered. E-tailers should not pay invoices until all the goods ordered are received.

prompt: To identify the best combination of transportation routes and modes for optimum distribution effectiveness and costs, a supply chain manager would use a(n)
explanation: Distribution model. A distribution model is used to determine the best pattern of distribution across different carrier routes. It indicates the most cost-effective and fastest method of moving goods from one location to another. Inventory models aid in determining proper inventory levels. Queuing models involve the amount of time that customers wait in line. Game theory is used to predict how a competitor will react to various activities of a business.

prompt: Brick-and-clicks often collect information from each sales check about the items purchased in order to maintain accurate
choices: records to comply with federal law.
explanation: Unit inventory control records. The sales check usually contains information about the size and type of items purchased. Brick-and-clicks add this information to the unit inventory control records on a regular basis, preferably daily, in order to maintain accurate records. Accurate records help businesses keep the right mix of items in stock. Businesses do not use the information from sales checks to maintain credit files on customers or to comply with federal law. Economic incentives are monetary rewards for certain economic activities.

prompt: What is a brick-and-click's average inventory in dollars if it has annual sales of $240,000 and a stock turnover rate of 5?
explanation: $48,000. The stock turnover rate is the number of times stock is sold in a given period of time. A brick-and-click can use the stock turnover rate to determine its average inventory value in dollars. To calculate average inventory, divide the amount of annual sales by the stock turnover rate ($240,000 ÷ 5 = $48,000). Therefore, the brick-and-click has an average of $48,000 in inventory at all times.

prompt: Some countries are not able to tap their natural resources because they lack the necessary
explanation: Technology. Some countries are not able to tap their natural resources because they do not have the technology or the information and ability needed to use the technology. They lack the necessary equip-ment, knowledge, and trained personnel to apply technical methods. Demographics is information used to describe a population. Productivity is the amount and value of goods and services produced (outputs) from set amounts of resources (inputs). Entrepreneurs are the people who organize or start a business and assume the risks.

prompt: One of the problems of a communist-command economic system often is
explanation: Product quality. Since workers in a communist-command economic system are usually paid by the number of goods they produce, rather than by the hour, they are more interested in the quantity of items produced than in their quality. Product quality suffers and the goods produced are often inferior. Total employment seldom exists. Most businesses are owned by the government rather than by private individuals. There is no competition.

prompt: What type of economic resource consists of individuals who use their skills in a particular job or task?
explanation: Human resources. Human resources include all of the men and women in the workforce. Capital goods are manufactured goods used in the production of other goods and services. Division of labor involves workers' being specialized by task. Natural resources are those resources produced by nature.

prompt: Which of the following transactions would be counted in the gross domestic product:
choices: A bakery purchases 50 pounds of sugar.
A florist purchases plants from a nursery.
A restaurant purchases meat from a wholesaler.
explanation: A customer purchases a sweater. This is an example of a personal consumption expenditure. Personal consumption expenditures include the final market value of all services and new and used goods purchased for consumption by individuals and nonprofit institutions. In the case of the restaurant, the florist, and the bakery, the purchases will be resold to consumers, and that value will be counted in GDP.

prompt: The advantage of e-commerce to small online marketers is that it gives them access to
explanation: International customers. Online marketing allows businesses to make their goods and services available to customers throughout the world. By creating a page on the Internet, even small businesses make it possible for people in other countries to see their products and place orders. The impact on international trade is significant because businesses that previously sold only to local customers can now sell to anyone who has access to a computer. E-commerce involves selling online rather than providing access to local manufac-turers, specialized vendors, or potential investors.

prompt: One way that businesses use electronic, computerized banking services is to
explanation: Pay invoices. One way that businesses use electronic, computerized banking services, such as electronic funds transfer (EFT), is to pay invoices. A business can use its computer system to access its bank account and electronically transfer funds to a vendor's account in order to pay invoices. This technology gives a busi-ness immediate access to its financial information and enables it to complete banking transactions quickly. Businesses do not use electronic, computerized banking services to order supplies or to reduce taxes. This type of technology often eliminates the need for businesses to write checks.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit to e-businesses of being able to purchase on credit:
explanation: Maintaining inventory levels. Maintaining inventory levels that will meet customers' needs is essential to the success of a business. If the e-business finds itself short of stock at a time when it is also short of cash, it may use credit to buy more. The other alternatives are benefits to businesses of extending credit to customers.

prompt: Wholesaler X purchases $50,000 worth of stock from Supplier Y and is not obligated to pay for the stock until 30 days after the date of the invoice. This is an example of
explanation: Trade credit. Trade credit is short-term, unsecured credit provided by suppliers to their customers. When a business uses equity financing, stock is sold to shareholders as a means of raising capital. Debt financing occurs when funds are borrowed.

prompt: Before beginning to assess marketing-information needs, an online business first needs to accurately
explanation: Define the problem. Before they can begin to decide what type of information they need to obtain, online businesses first need to accurately define the problem. If businesses are not completely sure of the problem, they will not be able to find information that will help them to solve it. The process of clearly defining the problem enables businesses to pinpoint the exact type of marketing information that will provide the answers they need. Once businesses have defined the problem, they might decide to conduct research that could include sampling the population. Businesses analyze the data after they collect it.

prompt: A large software corporation wants to gather information on its biggest competitor's product development plans. Should the corporation advertise and hold interviews for nonexistent jobs in order to get information from the competitor's employees?
choices: Yes, any method of gathering information is fair.
No, this strategy for gathering information is unethical.
No, the competitor's employees probably have no useful information.
Yes, employees would share information if they thought they would be hired.
explanation: No, this strategy for gathering information is unethical. It is unethical to advertise and interview for jobs that do not exist in order to get information from a competitor's employees. The competitor's employees may indeed have useful information and may be willing to share it in order to secure a job, but this method of gathering information is neither fair nor ethical.

prompt: Many Internet businesses obtain information about who their customers are and what they purchase by using a(n)
explanation: Online tracking system. Many Internet businesses use online tracking software that gathers a variety of information about customers such as their names, what they purchase, how often they access the site, when they access the site, etc. Businesses use this information to tailor their web sites to the needs and pref-erences of their customers. The information businesses obtain by using an online tracking system helps them to better market their products to the customers who are most likely to buy. A marketing strategy is a plan of action for achieving marketing goals and objectives. Autoresponder is a computer program that automatically returns a specified message to anyone who e-mailed a particular address. Businesses do not use a distribution manager to obtain information about their customers.

prompt: Computer businesses often obtain marketing information that identifies potential threats from competitors during the process of conducting
explanation: Environmental scans. Environmental scanning is the process of tracking external changes that affect a computer business and its market. Businesses often conduct scans of external environments, such as social, economic, political, and competitive, in order to identify changes or threats that may have an impact on their operations. During this process, businesses might identify potential threats from competitors, such as new goods and services, additional locations, lower prices, or aggressive advertising. The marketing information obtained from environmental scans will help businesses to deal with potential threats and make necessary changes in order to remain competitive. Operational reviews evaluate a business's internal operations. Developmental tests are intended to evaluate new goods and services. Governmental surveys are conducted by government agencies.

prompt: One reason why e-businesses often use databases to analyze information about customers is to
explanation: Make predictions. A database is a collection of facts and information arranged in a logical order so that it can be accessed and used when needed. E-businesses often maintain a vast amount of information about customers in databases and analyze the information to make predictions about how customers will respond in the future. For example, businesses might analyze customers' purchases to predict the products they will, or will not, buy in the future and the amount they are likely to spend. A business might use this information to make changes in its products based on what customers were buying. Businesses use spreadsheet software programs to prepare invoices and manage finances. Businesses use word-processing programs to prepare reports.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of an effective marketing report:
explanation: Provides clear interpretation of findings. One of the primary functions of a marketing report is to clearly and accurately interpret the research findings. Businesses conduct research in order to obtain information that will help them solve problems and make marketing decisions. An effective marketing report should interpret technical or complex information in such a way that it is easy for others to read and understand. An effective report logically interprets and summarizes the research findings and offers recommendations. Marketing reports do not need to contain the names of contributing editors, include industry overview information, and explain the role of executive management in order to be effective unless these topics are related to the specific research questions.

prompt: What do many online businesses use as a means of identifying their target markets?
explanation: Opt-in offers. Opt-in offers give potential customers the opportunity to decide if they want to receive infor-mation from online businesses. For example, a business might provide a place on its web site for users to sign up to receive e-mails about upcoming specials or discounts. These people have indicated an interest in the business and its products by opting to receive information; therefore, the business would consider them part of its target market. Online businesses do not identify their target markets through banner ads, chat rooms, or chain-mail lists.

prompt: The Internet company projected that its sales would increase significantly over the next few years, and it decided to
explanation: Hire more workers. One of the ways Internet businesses use sales forecasts is in determining whether or not to hire more workers. A projected sales increase would support the hiring of additional employees. A forecast for increased sales would tell a business not to raise its prices, lower inventory levels, or borrow operating funds.

prompt: One reason why marketing-information managers often monitor their competitors' web sites is to
explanation: Obtain data about new products. A business's web site contains volumes of information designed to attract customers and encourage them to buy. However, this information is also available to competitors. Conse-quently, marketing-information managers often monitor their competitors' web sites to obtain data about new products that competitors might be selling. This data might indicate the characteristics and features of the products as well as pricing information. Businesses might use this information to develop similar products or to update existing products. Although businesses post a lot of information on their web sites, they usually do not include information about inventory turnover rates, current sales records, or regional economic factors.

prompt: What approach to sales forecasting is being used by an online business that starts the process by preparing a sales forecast for the company as a whole?
explanation: Top-down. The top-down approach to sales forecasting involves starting the sales forecasting process by preparing an overall forecast for the entire company. It is also called the breakdown approach. The build-up, or bottom-up, approach involves starting the sales forecasting process by gathering individual forecasts that may be combined, or built up, into a forecast for the entire company. The Delphi technique is a sales fore-casting method, rather than an approach, and it combines internal and external expert opinion. Working capital is cash available for the business to use, or put to work, in its day-to-day operations.

prompt: One way to evaluate the performance of an e-business's marketing plan is to compare the marketing objectives with the
explanation: Actual results. E-businesses evaluate the performance of their marketing plans by comparing the actual results with the marketing objectives. A business would consider its marketing plan to be successful if its performance meets or exceeds the objectives. If the objectives were not met, a business would take correc-tive measures to solve the problem. Options are alternatives or other ways of accomplishing tasks. Market conditions are the economic circumstances of the market in which a firm does business. Sales policies are the general rules concerning selling activities.

prompt: Workers who like to set their own goals, exercise their creativity, and be free of control by a supervisor would be most comfortable working for a(n) __________ leader.
explanation: Laissezfaire. Persons in creative occupations who need free rein and only general guidance perform best under a laissezfaire leader. Democratic and authoritarian styles provide more structure and control than laissezfaire. There is no style of leadership classified as republican.

prompt: A positive result of handling customer complaints properly is that it will
explanation: Promote goodwill. Goodwill is a positive feeling a person has toward an online business. Properly settling complaints will promote goodwill, which may increase sales for the business. Increased returns and increased markdowns are negative outcomes of handling complaints improperly. Handling complaints properly does not affect objections—customers' reasons for not buying.

prompt: A competitive and well-designed compensation plan is important to an Internet business because it helps the business to
explanation: Retain qualified employees. An Internet business with a competitive and well-designed compensation plan often is able to attract and retain qualified employees. Compensation is an important factor to employees who often will seek other positions if they are not satisfied with their benefits package. Furthermore, employees who receive fair compensation usually are motivated to perform well and do a superior job. Businesses benefit from offering good compensation plans because it is less expensive to retain qualified employees than to continually hire and train new employees. Compensation plans do not help businesses to evaluate employee performance, establish retirement programs, or develop promotion policies.

prompt: One benefit of establishing a promotionfromwithin policy is that it
choices: reduces the need for ongoing training.
explanation: Increases employee loyalty. A commitment to the promotion of internal job candidates motivates employees to prepare for promotional opportunities and leads to more loyal employees. However, the most qualified people might be external candidates. Promoting from within often reduces salary expense because external recruits may expect higher incomes. Promoting from within does not reduce the need for ongoing training.

prompt: A free source of prospective employees that is particularly helpful to small Internet companies who do not maintain human resource departments is a
explanation: Government employment agency. Government employment agencies are public employment agencies operated under federal guidelines. They are available to employers and employees, and they do not charge a fee for their services because they are supported by tax dollars. College placement bureaus work mainly with larger companies. Private employment agencies and classified advertisements are good sources of employees, but neither would be free.

prompt: Which of the following should be considered when selecting instructional methods for a training and development program:
explanation: The objectives to be accomplished. In selecting instructional methods, you should consider the objectives to be accomplished, costs associated with the method, time needed to develop the activity, and the characteris-tics/capabilities of the trainees. Some ways that a good training and development program can affect a busi-ness and its employees are to reduce the level of absenteeism, improve morale, and increase productivity; but these are not factors in determining the way in which the training will be delivered.

prompt: The most basic of human needs are __________ needs.
explanation: Physical. According to Maslow's hierarchy, physical needs must be met before any other needs. They include the need for food, water, and shelter. Safety needs are associated with personal security and pro-tection from harm. Social needs include the need to belong to a group, to develop relationships with other people, to feel accepted, and to receive affection. Selfesteem needs are needs for approval, recognition, respect from others, and self-respect.

prompt: The manager of a large online bookstore has decided to use a work team to help the company improve customer service. Members of the team have been asked to develop goals and objectives for the project. Having team members agree on the purpose of their project is a way to build ___________ to the team and its work.
explanation: Commitment. Asking team members to develop team goals, mission, and values is one method for enhanc-ing employees' commitment to the team. It helps team members understand how their work contributes to the team and overall company objectives. Communication and creativity are important components of suc-cessful teams. Conflict is a team issue that may develop and require conflict resolution measures.

prompt: A business expense such as utilities is classified as a(n) __________ expense.
explanation: Fixed. A business's operating expenses are divided into fixed and variable costs. Fixed costs are business costs that are not affected by changes in sales volume. Variable costs change with changes in sales volume. Elastic is a term used to describe consumer demand that changes according to changes in price. Break-even is the point at which the business has recovered the expense of producing and/or selling a prod-uct and begins to make a profit.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a cost that is often unique to e-commerce:
explanation: Creating web sites. E-commerce businesses either create their own web sites or buy space on a commercial online service. There are costs associated with both because businesses often hire professionals to create appealing web sites and then update them on a regular basis. If the businesses buy space on an online service, there are annual fees and possibly creative charges. Businesses need to consider these costs because they may be significant over time. Creating web sites is more unique to e-commerce than to other types of businesses because not all businesses have web sites. However, many businesses today purchase computers and pay data processors. Businesses involved in e-commerce usually purchase software rather than develop it.

prompt: An Internet business negotiates a three-year lease on office space for $2,250 per month which will increase 2% per month in the second year and 3% over the second-year rate in the third year. What will the business's monthly rent be in the third year?
explanation: $2,363.85. When Internet businesses negotiate long-term leases, they often negotiate the amount of increase from year to year. In this example, the rent will increase 2% the second year. To calculate the monthly rent for the second year, multiply the first year rate by the rate of increase ($2,250 x 2% or .02 = $45), and add that amount to the first year rate ($2,250 + $45 = $2,295). The third year, monthly rent will increase 3% over the second year's rate of $2,295. To calculate that amount, multiply the second year rate by the rate of increase ($2,295 x 3% or .03 = $68.85), and add that amount to the second year rate ($2,295.00 + $68.85 = $2,363.85).

prompt: Which of the following is a factor specific to a business that an e-tailer should understand in order to plan an effective marketing program:
explanation: Competition. Competition is different for each e-business. Knowing who your competitors are gives you the opportunity to offer advantages they do not provide. Learning who your competitors are—their strengths and their weaknesses—will be basic to planning your competitive advantage and marketing strategies. Technol-ogy, the economy, and regulations are factors that affect all businesses.

prompt: The ability to generate unique ideas, approaches, and solutions is called
explanation: Creativity. Creativity is a personal trait involving imagination and original thought. Determination means commitment to the accomplishment of some purpose or goal. Integrity means honesty or conformity to established personal standards. Interest is concern for or excitement about something/someone.

prompt: Advantages to online business owners of reading trade journals are that they contain reports by industry experts and
explanation: Current product information. One of the values of trade journals is the uptodate product and technology information that they provide. Trade publications keep online business owners and their employees informed about their industry. Advertising in trade journals is extensive and provides additional information. Trade journals are written for specific groups of workers/industries and do not have articles about other industries or articles directed to consumers.

prompt: An Internet business priced a new product well below the current market price. Sales were very low because many customers believed the product was of poor quality because of its low price. This seller did not set a __________ price.
explanation: Realistic. A realistic price is a price customers perceive to be appropriate for the product. Low prices are often perceived as indicating poor quality. Flexible prices are prices that are adjusted because of changes in economic circumstances. Competitive prices are in line with other businesses' prices. There was no indica-tion in this situation that the product's price was not legal.

prompt: A goal of many e-businesses that affects their pricing is
explanation: Obtaining market share. Marketers may use selling price to obtain a share of the market, to enlarge the share they already have, or to maintain that share. E-businesses with profit-oriented pricing try to maximize their profits by setting prices that will bring in the maximum amount of profit in the shortest time. Variable costs cannot be stabilized since by their nature they fluctuate with changes in sales. Cooperative advertising is funds provided to retailers by the producers of goods to help pay the retailers' advertising expenses and is not dependent on prices.

prompt: One of the main disadvantages of using the cost-based method for setting base price is that it fails to take into consideration
explanation: Competitors' prices. The cost-based method for setting base price considers the costs involved in producing and marketing a product. This method does not take into consideration the prices that competitors are charging for similar products. A business using the cost-based method may set a price that is higher than a competitor's price. As a result, the product may not sell because customers can purchase the same item for a lower price from a competitor. Businesses using the cost-based method for setting price take into consid-eration marketing charges, production costs, and operating expenses.

prompt: Calculate the amount of a brick-and-click's total variable costs from the following information: Mortgage payments $ 15,000 Sales promotion 5,500 Utilities 3,600 Employees' wages 80,000 Owner's salary 60,000 Insurance 2,900 Cost of goods 125,000
explanation: $130,500. In order to determine total variable costs, you must first classify the costs as fixed or variable. Variable costs are costs that change according to changes in sales volume. In this case, they include sales promotion and cost of goods. Add these individual costs to determine total variable costs ($5,500 + $125,000 = $130,500).

prompt: Online businesses should set their selling prices at a level that will
choices: be lower than that of competitors.
be equal to the cost of goods.
ensure a high percent of profit.
explanation: Cover expected markdowns and expenses. Online businesses can prevent markdowns and expenses from cutting into their net profit by setting prices that include allowances for markdowns and expenses. Setting the original selling price equal to cost would result in a loss for the business. Undercutting competitors' prices may be possible in some cases but is unwise if it reduces profits. Setting prices that will ensure a high profit may result in prices that are too high to foster sales.

prompt: What is one technique that businesses can use to identify and correct web-site problems?
explanation: Troubleshooting. Troubleshooting involves looking for web-site problems, such as broken links and slow-loading graphics, and fixing the problems once they are identified. Troubleshooting is important because problems on the site can create a negative impression of the business and cause visitors to think that the business has a careless attitude. Global navigation is a system for making certain pages always accessible to visitors by including the same links on every single page within a site. Brainstorming is a creative thinking technique involving the identification of as many different ideas as possible during a certain time frame. Affiliate marketing is the process of promoting and selling another business's products on a web site in exchange for a sales commission.

prompt: When an online bath and soap store uses its product wrapping to promote the preservation of an endangered animal species, it is engaging in an ethical practice called
explanation: Cause packaging. Cause packaging is using a product to promote a political or social issue. For example, The Body Shop places wording on its product packaging that the company does not test its products on animals. This indicates that the company does not believe in testing products on animals, which is a very controversial and ethical issue. Environmental labeling and provocative branding are not commonly used terms associated with packaging. Political lobbying is the act of trying to influence the attitudes and actions of legislative groups.

prompt: Consumer protection should be an important concern for Internet businesses because failure to comply with the laws
choices: increases the rate of new-product development.
explanation: Can lose the public's goodwill. Internet businesses that fail to comply with regulations run the risk of damaging their image and losing the public's goodwill. Since most lawsuits against a business are highly publicized, the public is made well aware that the company has apparently disregarded the well-being of consumers. Even when only one business in an industry has been charged, the effects of the bad publicity may have a negative effect on other businesses in the same industry. An important effect of government regulation is that it can increase a business's expenses. Failing to comply with consumer protection does not automatically mean that a business will fail. Complying with consumer-protection laws makes the research and development process for new products longer and thus more expensive.

prompt: If an item selling for $21 has a gross margin of $10, then the item's __________ is $11.
explanation: Cost to the e-tailer. Gross margin is the difference between an item's cost and its selling price. Since the selling price is $21, and gross margin is $10, $11 is the cost of the item to the e-tailer ($21 – $10 = $11). Not enough information is given to determine the operating expenses or profit percentage.

prompt: A specialty online boutique whose target market is the career woman with expensive taste would have a product mix with __________ assortment.
explanation: Narrow variety, deep. The terms used to describe the scope of a boutique's product mix include broad or narrow and shallow or deep. A product mix with narrow variety refers to a limited number of product lines. A deep assortment refers to a great many items in each product line. This boutique offers a great many items of clothing and accessories but only in a few product lines. A broad product mix offers many product lines. A shallow mix offers few items in the product line.

prompt: An important customer-service issue in e-commerce involves determining the best method to use to
explanation: Answer customers' questions. Providing service to online customers involves developing a method of answering their questions quickly and accurately. Customers often have questions about products, or the online business's privacy policies, or how to return purchases. Determining the best way to answer these questions is of major concern to online businesses because if customers are not satisfied with the service they receive, they probably will not buy from that business in the future. Advertising is not a customer-service issue. Online businesses usually do not bill customers but expect customers to pay for purchases when ordering. Maintaining inventory levels is a distribution issue.

prompt: Consumers tend to buy brands they feel good about because such purchases
choices: give them a sense of comfort.
are based on rational buying motives.
explanation: Give them a sense of comfort. Consumers associate brands with a certain price level, performance, or sense of comfort. When consumers feel good about brands, they buy them. This does not guarantee that they will always be totally satisfied since even the best brands occasionally produce a "lemon." Buying on the basis of feeling is an emotional buying motive, not a rational motive. Consumers are not interested in reinforcing the company's image.

prompt: Why is it important for a business to have its web site listed with major search engines and directories?
choices: To make it easy for users to find
To arrange for links on other sites
To have access to banner ads
To be able to distribute e-mail
explanation: To make it easy for users to find. Having a web site is not effective unless users are able to find and access it. To make it easy for users to find, businesses usually pay to have their sites listed with search engines and directories. When potential customers conduct a search using key words, the business's site will be listed. If customers have difficulty finding a business's web site, they often access other sites that are easy to find. The result might be that the business loses sales. Arranging for links on other sites is a way of promoting a web site. Businesses do not list their web sites with major search engines and directories to be able to dis-tribute e-mail or to have access to banner ads.

prompt: Should Internet businesses rely solely on their previous promotional mixes?
choices: No, promotional budgets decrease each year.
No, there may be other, more successful mixes to try.
Yes, there is usually one promotional mix that is best.
Yes, what has worked in the past will work in the future.
explanation: No, there may be other, more successful mixes to try. A promotional mix is a combination, or blend, of marketing communication channels that an Internet business uses to send its messages to consumers. A company should continually analyze its promotional mix in order to be sure it is using the most appropriate, efficient mix. In some cases, a promotional mix that has been successful in the past may continue to be successful in the future, but this is not always the case. There is no one promotional mix that is best for all businesses, and a promotional budget does not necessarily decrease each year.

prompt: What do advertising regulations usually require online businesses to disclose about the products they advertise?
explanation: Limitations. Certain products have limitations, such as producing side effects in some people or being poten-tially hazardous. When online businesses advertise these products, they are usually required to disclose the limitations so consumers can make an informed decision about whether to buy. Businesses that violate these regulations run the risk of being sued by consumers who were harmed by the products. Advertise-ments usually describe the benefits of the products and often contain endorsements. Advertisements often point out important features especially if they are hidden.

prompt: What do many businesses send by e-mail to customers who make online purchases?
explanation: Order confirmations. Customers who make online purchases often receive e-mail messages indicating that their orders are being processed and provide product tracking numbers. Businesses send e-mail confirma-tions to minimize the number of cancellations, returns, and telephone calls. Businesses usually do not e-mail customers with special requests, printed invoices, or cancellation notices.

prompt: Copywriters who are preparing advertising copy should avoid making __________ about competitors.
explanation: Negative comments. Copywriters should avoid writing negative copy, including negative comments about competitors or criticisms of their products. This kind of copy may trigger complaints of unfair practices. It may also get a negative reaction from some readers who feel a product can't be very good if the business has to promote it by tearing down competing products. If copywriters mention competitors in advertising copy, they should use precise statements, accurate remarks, and factual observations.

prompt: So Internet users can move easily through a web site and know where they are at all times within the web site, the web designer must carefully plan the
explanation: Navigation system. The navigation system refers to the method in which an Internet user moves through a web-site's pages to get from one location to another. The web-site designer should make it easy for users to know where they are at all times and be able to move to another page or site quickly and efficiently to lower the risk of frustration. The domain name is the business's web address. Although it is an important consid-eration in the overall web-site development process, it does not necessarily affect how well the users maneuver through the web site. The web-site reach refers to the percentage of the web users that visit a site during a set time period compared to all web users. Although management can estimate its reach, the web designers cannot control how many users visit a web site at any given time. Interaction refers to the flow of information between two sources. Interaction rate is not a term that is widely used in the e-commerce indus-try in relation to promotional efforts.

prompt: One reason why a business might pay to purchase multiple domain names is to
explanation: Account for typographical errors. A domain name represents a business's web address. Many businesses pay for additional domain names to increase their chances of being found and to account for typographical errors. For example, if a customer types in cdwearhouse.com instead of cdwarehouse.com, the customer will not find the correct web site. However, if the business owns both domain names, customers will find the business even though they type in the wrong web address. Businesses do not purchase multiple domain names to advertise on other web sites, provide high-speed connections, or display options for customers.

prompt: Any positive or negative mention of an Internet firm or its product in the mass media, other than in the form of a paid advertisement, is an example of
explanation: Publicity. Publicity is any nonpersonal presentation of ideas, goods, or services that is not paid for by the company that receives it. Positive publicity can benefit a company, while negative publicity can do it harm. Positioning is the perception of a company or a product in the minds of consumers. Personal selling is planned, personalized communication that influences purchase decisions and enhances future business opportunities. Special incentives are items such as premiums and free samples used to increase sales.

prompt: Mirror Research's periodically offering survey results on the Web to lure businesses to purchase reports is an example of
explanation: Sampling. Sampling provides potential customers with a free sample of the company's work in the hope of getting them to purchase future products. Personal selling involves the use of planned, personalized com-munication that influences purchase decisions and enhances future business opportunities. Product screen-ing is the process of considering each idea for a new product and discarding those that seem unworkable. Ecoupons are coupons provided online.

prompt: Providing a price reduction on a product by allowing the customer to redeem a section of an advertisement is an example of providing a
explanation: Coupon. Coupons offer customers a price reduction when they purchase the product referred to on the coupon. A directsales premium is a gift often given for participation in a sales demonstration. A factory pack is a gift made available with a purchase. A product sample is a small amount of a product given to potential customers.

prompt: The overall objectives of an e-tailer's promotional plan are to stimulate product demand and
explanation: Create a positive image. Promotion is defined as a marketing function needed to communicate information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. The promotional plan is the framework for an e-tailer's promotional activities. Generally, the primary or overall objectives are to enhance or create a favorable image. Usually, a company that communicates a positive image is more likely to obtain and retain customers. By communicating information about products, images, or ideas, the company is trying to stimulate interest or create demand. Promotional mix is the combination of marketing communica-tion channels that a business uses to send its messages (advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, and publicity). Channel members are businesses or individuals who assist in moving goods and services from the producer to the consumer. Since each consumer has different personal values, it is not possible to con-struct a promotional plan that considers each individual's values.

prompt: What is one of the simplest promotional methods that a company can use to promote its web site?
choices: Adding a URL to all business materials
explanation: Adding a URL to all business materials. A URL serves much like a telephone number, giving people a way to contact the business. Adding a URL to all business materials is one of the simplest promotional methods there is. Possibilities include company letterhead, business cards, clothing, coffee mugs, displays, and so forth. Giving away something for free, advertising in national magazines, and operating an online discussion group are other promotional methods; but they are not as simple as adding a URL to all business materials.

prompt: A brick-and-click with an advertising department might sometimes hire an outside advertising agency because such agencies
choices: work for the media and/or suppliers.
receive massive discounts on media prices.
charge very low fees for special ads.
explanation: Have a more objective viewpoint. Outside agencies can offer the brick-and-click a fresh viewpoint for an ad campaign, but their fees are not low. Advertising agencies do not work for the media and/or suppliers. The agency's obligation lies with the customer and not the media. Most agencies receive an agency discount that may be passed on to the client, but it is not a massive amount.

prompt: Which of the following is the most cost-effective method of providing online customer support:
choices: Using e-mail to communicate with customers
Hiring employees to chat with customers online
Including helpful information on the business's web site
explanation: Including helpful information on the business's web site. It hardly costs the business anything to post a frequently asked questions page that provides information that customers commonly seek. All of the other alternatives involve hiring customer-service representatives to communicate with customers, which can cost the business a significant sum of money. For example, staff members with good writing skills would be needed to respond to e-mail inquiries and to chat with customers online. Also, customer-service representa-tives with good oral communication skills would be needed to answer telephones at a customer call center.

prompt: The clientele of an e-business refers to its
explanation: Repeat customers. Clientele is a body of customers upon which an organization can rely for considerable repeat business. Creditors are those to whom an individual or a business owes money. Vendors are suppliers of goods, and preferred vendors are those from whom the business prefers to make purchases. Distribution channels are the paths that goods and services take from the producer to the ultimate consumer or industrial user.

prompt: What type of computer software do businesses often use to analyze numerical sales information?
explanation: Spreadsheet. Spreadsheet computer programs (e.g., Excel, Quatro Pro) are used to organize and calculate numerical information. Spreadsheets can be used in sales to track and evaluate sales volume and sales dollars. Word-processing software is primarily used to create text documents such as contracts, memos, and letters. Presentation software is generally used by salespeople when making a sales or product presen-tation to customers. Graphic and design software is often used to create catalogs, brochures, and other professional illustrations.

prompt: What legal action can a consumer take if a product has been misrepresented by a brick-and-click or salesperson?
explanation: File a lawsuit. A lawsuit occurs when one party takes another party to a court of law to resolve a conflict or disagreement. Often, lawsuits are filed to obtain financial reimbursement for various activities, including product misrepresentation or breach of warranty. Although requesting reimbursement for the product is possible, it is only a legal action if a lawsuit or petition is filed. Conducting an investigation is not necessarily a legal action. Government officials generally establish legislation, not consumers.

prompt: Which of the following is a social factor that often influences a consumer's buying behavior:
explanation: Marital status. A variety of social factors often influence a consumer's buying behavior. One of these factors is marital status. Consumers who are married and part of a family usually make buying decisions based on what the family group wants and needs. These buying decisions are different than the ones that a single person might make. For example, a married man with three small children will make different buying decisions than a single man with no dependents. Basic needs, such as food and drink, are physiological factors that influence buying behavior. Attitude is the way a person looks at life. A belief is a person's opinion about something.

prompt: Suggestion selling can benefit the brick-and-click by increasing
explanation: Profits. The business benefits from suggestion selling because it increases sales, which means additional profit can be earned and inventory can be reduced more quickly. Suggestion selling benefits employees by increasing their commissions. Suggestion selling is not a factor in follow-up.

prompt: Web-page design salespeople who ask themselves if they let their customers know how much they appreciate their business are using the technique of
explanation: Evaluating follow-up. Web-page design salespeople evaluate their follow-up in order to determine its effectiveness. Asking themselves questions about their follow-up helps them to determine their strengths and weaknesses and make any necessary adjustments. Handling objections is the technique of settling a point of difference between a customer and a salesperson that may prevent a sale. Suggestion selling is the technique in which the salesperson attempts to increase the customer's purchase by suggesting additional items after the original decision to buy has been made. Sales training is a systematic process for enabling salespeople to acquire the attitudes, knowledge, and skills that are needed in order to attain organizational goals.

prompt: Prospecting should be a(n) __________ process.
explanation: Ongoing. Prospecting should be done every day rather than occasionally or on a one-time basis. All information used in prospecting should be accurate and up-to-date. Prospecting is not optional because it is necessary.

prompt: One reason why it is important for the first sentence in a sales letter to gain the reader's attention is because most sales letters are
explanation: Unsolicited. In most cases, sales letters are written and mailed to people who have not requested informa-tion. The letters are an attempt to interest people in certain goods or services and persuade them to buy. These letters must attract the reader's attention quickly so the person will continue reading and concentrate on the sales message. One way to do this is to open with an attention-getting sentence. Many sales letters provide necessary information and give realistic explanations of the value of the goods or services being offered. Most sales letters are grammatical.

prompt: What do many Internet retailers plan to offer in order to sell effectively online?
explanation: Large assortments. Internet retailers often are able to offer large assortments of products because they do not need to inventory those products. Internet retailers are able to buy from manufacturers or intermediaries on an "as needed" basis and resell those items to customers who have already placed an order. For example, an online bookstore can obtain a book from a publisher when a customer orders it. The bookstore does not keep the book in stock and is able to purchase any book that the customer orders. This option makes it possible for an online bookstore to offer thousands of book titles that a traditional store would be unable to keep in stock. Offering expensive products will not necessarily enable an Internet retailer to sell effectively online. Convenient hours and multiple locations are considerations of traditional retailing rather than online retailing.

prompt: Which of the following is one of the main responsibilities of a sales manager for a web-maintenance company:
explanation: Recruit qualified staff. One of the main responsibilities of a sales manager is to recruit, select, and hire qualified individuals who will be the most effective salespeople for the web-maintenance business. Having the right people on staff is the best way to sell the business's products. Qualified salespeople often are able to sell, even under difficult situations. Sales managers usually are not responsible for making sales calls, prospecting for clientele, or scheduling demonstrations.

prompt: One difference between online consumer and organizational buying behavior is that consumers often
choices: negotiate terms and methods of delivery.
rely on family members when making decisions.
sign long-term contracts with online businesses.
explanation: Rely on family members when making decisions. The buying behavior of the ultimate consumer is different than the buying behavior of organizations. One main difference is that consumers often rely on family members when making decisions about what to buy and when to buy. Consumers are influenced by many groups including family, friends, coworkers, and others. Therefore, consumers might buy a certain product from a specific online business because family members or others recommended the business. Organiza-tions that buy online often develop relationships with the online business and expect the business to provide support and information. Because the volume of buying is often much larger, organizations frequently sign long-term contracts with online businesses and negotiate terms and methods of delivery. This makes it possible for organizations to reorder online and receive the agreed on price and terms.

prompt: Which of the following do Internet companies often call upon to assist with sales training:
explanation: Consultants. Internet companies often call upon consultants, or outside specialists, to assist with sales training. Consultants may establish and administer a customized program or design sales training to be implemented by others in the organization. This can minimize training costs since it is purchased on an asneeded basis. Companies do not obtain assistance with sales training from stockholders or competitors. A subsidiary is a company that is wholly owned and controlled by another company.
